clue.text: Old man, German, nods and regularly drops off

indicators.note: every other letter falls away from these words, leaving the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Grandfather, a German, nods off in his chair now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' looks like a G on its own, but it is part of the run read alternately: GeRmAn NoDs AnD.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term for a grandfather, or more loosely any elderly man.

clue.text: Great man has guns to hand

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun
by in the sense of nearby, within reach

explanation.surface: An important figure who keeps firearms close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' looks like praise; it is the title of Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay, the title character of Fitzgerald's novel, is called Great in its title.

clue.text: A painful condition oppresses one rodent

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of, weighing down, the next

parts.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An agonising ailment weighs heavily on a single rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a burrowing South American rodent related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Repeal bold move? Scandalous!

indicators.note: a move shifts things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daring repeal of a law is condemned as outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe conduct so bad it deserves strong condemnation, synonyms for shameful.

clue.text: American city, say, Sir Ken almost roused

indicators.note: stirred up, which in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means

indicators.note: the surname is one letter short of complete

parts.note: Sir Ken Dodd was a famous Liverpool comedian

explanation.surface: A US city, for instance, nearly stirred Sir Ken into action.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Ken Dodd was a British comedian famed for tickling sticks; DOD plus EG are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodge City, Kansas, a Wild West cattle town, gives the name of this place in the States.

clue.text: Piece of music has to carry a sound

indicators.note: the word here tells the solver to say the phrase out loud and listen

parts.note: to carry something is to cart it, so this phrase becomes 'to cart a'

explanation.surface: A piece of music must convey a particular sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noun the music carries; it is the instruction to say 'to cart a' out loud, which in a non-rhotic British accent matches the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard composition, a kind of musical work.

clue.text: I hurl stones, but three caught surprisingly

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement of the letters is signalled

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A stone-thrower complains that, against the odds, three were caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A trebuchet was a medieval siege engine, a catapult that flung heavy stones at walls.

clue.text: Players squint

definitions.meaning: the actors in a play collectively
a dated term for a slight squint in the eye

explanation.definitionFit: The company of actors in a production, and an old word for a turned eye.

clue.text: Gone to outside broadcast carrying disc and record player: just as well

indicators.note: the first pair holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: ago means gone by, in the past
a disc is round, like the letter O
a DJ is a disc jockey, who plays records

explanation.surface: A radio crew goes out on location with a record and a disc jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record player' suggests a turntable but means a disc jockey; 'to' simply joins the first two pieces, and 'carrying' sets the disc and jockey between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom said of a fortunate circumstance, meaning it is lucky or fortunate that something happened.

clue.text: In prayer, deified sun, gazing up a little

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards
only a small part of these words is taken, lying within them

explanation.surface: Someone worships the sun as a god, glancing up at it briefly in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lamb of God, a Latin invocation recited in the Mass, is a liturgical prayer.

clue.text: Men replaced in best part of a squadron

indicators.note: the turned soldiers are put in among the letters of the word for best

parts.note: the best is the top

indicators.note: put back the other way round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are swapped into the elite section of a squadron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best part' reads as one phrase, but 'best' gives the outer letters and 'part of a squadron' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a cavalry or armoured unit, a subdivision of a squadron.

clue.text: Carpet to decorate with feathers

parts.note: to dress a shop window or table is to decorate it
down is the soft fine feathering of birds

explanation.surface: Trimming a rug with feathers, an odd piece of home decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like the floor covering; here it is the verb, to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to reprimand them, the same as giving them a severe telling-off.

clue.text: Repressed, although more vigorous

parts.note: although and but both introduce a contrast
toned up means made firmer and more vigorous

explanation.surface: Someone inhibited, though becoming more energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a person who keeps feelings tightly controlled and is socially reserved, as if clothing were fastened to the neck.

clue.text: Fish day

definitions.meaning: ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family; the plural gives the letters
a fixed day in the Roman calendar, the 15th of March, May, July and October, the 13th otherwise

explanation.surface: Fish day: a day for eating fish, like a Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of a carp-family fish, and also the Roman mid-month date best known from Caesar's assassination.

clue.text: Trojan widow even having love affair, dropping name and securing husband

parts.note: 'and' can carry the sense of even, as in 'and with that'

indicators.note: the shortened affair holds the next letter fast inside it
the abbreviation is let fall out of the word

parts.note: a romance is a love affair

explanation.surface: A widow from Troy took a lover, abandoned her name and caught another husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector's wife in Homer, widowed when Achilles killed him at Troy.

clue.text: A new vault over the poles? Much more

indicators.note: the vaulted roof stretches over the following letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a dome is an arched vault
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A fresh vaulting leap right over the earth's poles, an absurdly ambitious jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' suggests a pole vault; it is the arched roof, a DOME, put over THE plus N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom used for a quantity exceeding what was stated, a great deal extra.

clue.text: Abroad, met implausibly wonderful man

indicators.note: something improbable signals the letters are scrambled into an unlikely order

explanation.surface: On holiday overseas she met an impossibly perfect man.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a very attractive man, the ideal partner of one's dreams.

clue.text: Spilling blobs, make mess on small disk

parts.note: a platter is a flat round plate, and also slang for a gramophone record

explanation.surface: Dripping messily over a little plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash or spray drops of liquid around untidily, making a mess.

clue.text: One set of books bulky to lift as a whole

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word means reading it upwards

parts.note: large and bulky both mean big

explanation.surface: One complete set of account books is too heavy to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral describes something essential to, or forming, a complete entity.

clue.text: Bodybuilder's fiendish quiz question?

parts.note: a worker who hammers car body sections into shape repairs bodywork, and a question so hard it defeats a quiz panel would also earn the name

explanation.surface: A gym enthusiast poses a devilishly hard trivia question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bodybuilder' suggests a muscleman; it means someone who repairs car bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who beats dented vehicle panels back into shape, and punningly a question that beats a quiz team.

clue.text: Determined where nomads live?

definitions.meaning: firmly resolved, fixed on a purpose
wanderers sleep under canvas, inside a tent, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Resolved on doing something, and split in two it says where a wandering herder sleeps.

clue.text: No black children regularly rejected their raw seafood

indicators.note: this letter is taken away from the word for children

parts.note: boys are male children
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: every other letter is thrown out, keeping the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Children refuse their raw seafood platter, with no black bits.
explanation.definitionFit: These shellfish are commonly eaten raw on the half shell.

clue.text: God has no time for a break

indicators.note: the following item is missing from the word for a break

parts.note: a rest is a break from activity

explanation.surface: A deity too busy to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war, Mars to the Romans.

clue.text: Monastery gambling with a million that is shrewdly invested

indicators.note: taking a gamble, the letters are thrown about and reshuffled

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for a million

explanation.surface: Monks wagering a million on the markets with clever investments.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrase for funds placed by experienced, well-informed investors, money expected to do well.

clue.text: One up, we hear — on course for this cup?

indicators.note: the words point to a match in sound with what follows

parts.note: a rider is one up on a horse, mounted

explanation.surface: A golfer one hole up on the course, heading for a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One up' looks like a golf match score; it is someone in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf's Ryder Cup is the biennial Europe versus USA team contest played on a course.

clue.text: No end of religion for this girl

indicators.note: the final letter of the faith is removed

parts.note: Islam is a world religion

explanation.surface: A girl devoted endlessly to her faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Isla is a girl's given name, popular in Scotland.

clue.text: Prime cut available to buy outside hotel entrance

indicators.note: the word is shortened by removing its final letter

parts.note: three is a prime number

indicators.note: the word for on sale goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: sold in the sense of offered for sale, as in 'sold here'
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Choice cuts of meat on sale near a hotel's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime cut' reads as best meat; 'Prime' is THREE and 'cut' removes its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: The sill or doorway one crosses to go in, the point of entry to a building.

clue.text: Top of a short run

indicators.note: the name is curtailed, losing its final letter

parts.note: the Cresta Run is a famous toboggan run at St Moritz in Switzerland

explanation.surface: The summit reached at the top of a brief sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' calls up running; it is the Cresta Run, the toboggan course in St Moritz, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A crest is the highest point of a hill or wave, its summit.

clue.text: Robin perhaps flying in later

indicators.note: a word of movement suggests the letters are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: A robin, say, takes to the air later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robin' suggests the bird, which 'flying' supports; it is the Reliant Robin, a British three-wheeled car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Robin was a model made by this British carmaker, so it is an example of the make.

clue.text: Tenant accepting lease finally to regain admittance

indicators.note: the tenant takes in the next letter, which goes within the word

parts.note: a renter is a tenant who pays rent

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A tenant who signs the lease at last gets back into the property.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back in or go in again, which is what regaining admittance amounts to.
